chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Zur'ah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When you sit in the second rak'ah, say: 'In the name of Allah and by Allah, and all praise is for Allah, and the best of names are for Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, whom He sent with the truth as a bearer of good news and a warner before the Hour. I bear witness that You are the best Lord and that Muhammad is the best Messenger. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and accept his intercession for his ummah and raise his rank.'
Then praise Allah two or three times, then stand up.

When you sit in the fourth [rak'ah], say: 'In the name of Allah and by Allah, and all praise is for Allah, and the best of names are for Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, whom He sent with the truth as a bearer of good news and a warner before the Hour. I bear witness that You are the best Lord and that Muhammad is the best Messenger.'
All greetings are for Allah, and the pure, good, pure, morning, fragrant, complete, gentle blessings are for Allah. Whatever is pure, sanctified, purified, refined, and clear belongs to Allah.

And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, whom He sent with the truth as a bearer of good news and a warner before the Hour. I bear witness that my Lord is the best Lord and that Muhammad is the best Messenger.
"That the Hour is coming, of which there is no doubt, and that Allah will raise those who are in the graves."
"All praise is for Allah who guided us to this, and we would not have been guided if Allah had not guided us."
"All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds."

O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and grant peace upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and have mercy on Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings and mercy upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.

O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and 'Forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not put in our hearts any resentment for those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.'
O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and grant me Paradise and deliver me from the Fire.

O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and forgive the believing men and believing women, 'And for whoever enters my house in a state of faith, and for the believing men and women, and do not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.'

Then say: 'Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon the prophets and messengers of Allah. Peace upon Gabriel and Michael and the near angels. Peace upon Muhammad ibn Abdillah, the seal of the prophets, there is no prophet after him.'
And peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah.
Then you give the salam.' And the minimum that suffices from the Tashahhud is the two testimonies.
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications to recite while sitting in prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the comprehensive Tashahhud recitation, emphasizing the Shia practice of appending extensive supplications and Quranic verses after the initial testimony of faith. It highlights the theological significance of seeking intercession (*shafa'ah*) and acknowledging the Prophet's role as a mercy, reflecting the devotional depth characteristic of Imami jurisprudence.
